_readme: The only place a content date may be overridden. src/build/content-dates.mjs
computes datePublished and dateModified from git on every build; this file
supplies the three things git cannot know. Read that module's header first.
history: earlier git paths for a page, for lineage git cannot detect. Phase 1
flattened the repo and Phases 3.3a-ii/3.3b extracted each page's <main> into
src/templates/, and a 24-line extract of a 300-line page does not look like a
rename to git. Without these, every calculator would claim to have been
published on the day it was extracted. Each path is queried with --follow and
the results unioned, so listing the immediate predecessor is enough.
mechanicalCommits: commits that touched page files without changing what a
reader sees. They are skipped when picking dateModified. Going forward the
mechanism is a 'Content-Change: none' trailer in the commit message and
nothing needs adding here; this list seeds the commits made before that
trailer existed. Getting one wrong only makes a dateModified newer than it
should be.
dates: a literal override, which wins outright. For the case where git is
right about the file and wrong about the content. Every entry states why.
This file has been lost three times as a hand-edit to a generated file (see
docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-08-16/08-29/09-21). It is real committed input now, so
regenerating dates can no longer discard it.

textHashes: the visible-text hash of every page whose date comes from an entry in "dates" above, recorded beside the dateModified it was taken under. check-build check 15 fails when a page's text no longer matches: bump the date, then run scripts/record-text-hashes.mjs. It vouches for changes from 2026-09-24 onward, not for history (DECISIONS 2026-09-24).

mechanicalCommits.db21e9c: refactor(dates): the commit that introduced this mechanism. Its only touch on a tracked path is three comment lines in src/data/geo-aeo.js, renaming generate-geo-aeo.mjs to src/build/geo.mjs. It carries no Content-Change trailer and could not list its own hash here, so on the first build after it landed /faqs and all eight service-area pages claimed dateModified 2026-09-22. Check 9 did not fire: nine of seventy is under its threshold, correctly, because nine genuinely changed pages is plausible. See docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-09-22.

privacy-policy.html.why: THE FOURTH TIME THIS HAS BEEN LOST. See docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-08-16/08-29/09-21: three times a sitewide mechanical commit became the most recent touch on this file and pushed dateModified to a date its content did not change, three times it was hand-reverted to 2026-07-23, three times the next script run discarded it. Moving the computation to build time lost it again, on the first run, which is exactly what this file exists to stop. The terms of this page last changed 2026-07-23. Do not let a nav edit say otherwise.

terms-of-service.html.why: Same as privacy-policy.html above, and lost on the same three occasions.

__datafile__src/data/services.js.why: Git tracks files, not the services inside one. Every service shares services.js's history, so each claims the file's creation date. 2026-06-01 is when the earliest of them actually shipped; the file itself was created 2026-07-02, which made every service look newer than it is. See docs/archive/FINDINGS.md #7 — kitchen-remodeling is the clearest case, added 2026-08-29 and claiming 2026-07-02. Per-service dates need per-object history, which git does not have; this at least stops the oldest services from being backdated forward. Since Phase 6.3 a service can carry its own dates as a __service__<id> entry below; the Tier 1 lead offers do.

__datafile__src/data/guides-cost.js.why: Pinned 2026-09-25 at the date git gave it that day, so the 11 cost guides and the /cost hub can be dated one page at a time. Git tracks the file, not the guides inside it: before this, adding or editing one entry re-dated every page this file renders. A page whose text changes now takes its own entry, keyed by its file (e.g. "cost/<slug>.html"), and check 15 fails until it has one. Do not move this pair to date a single page.
